card.name: Spot before a spelled-out tablet count
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a small word right after a dose amount, where a spelled-out number such as one, two or four comes next, as in "(one tablet)". Seen mostly in dose-reduction tables.

modes.label: Bracket after dose
modes.description: An opening parenthesis after an mg amount, just before a written-out count of tablets or capsules.
modes.example: 384 mg (two tablets) orally twice a day 192 mg<< (>>one tablet) orally twice a day

modes.label: Slash or asterisk after daily dose
modes.description: A symbol after a mg/day figure in a dose-reduction table, before a spelled-out number of tablets.
modes.example: 200 mg tablets First dose reduction 400 mg/day two 200 mg tablets Second dose reduction 200 mg/day<< *>> one 200 mg tablet *

modes.label: Before a number in prose
modes.description: A gap or the word day right before a number such as "something like 12" or "1".
modes.example: went before every Legislature for<< >>something like 12 years. When
